ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $7.07 Ryde voucher refund (unexempt detour mileage) for this RydeTAXI trip and note the RD-1 shortest-route breach; no account flag required (driver has 0 upheld route disputes).
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat is empty [F7]; the driver's statement [F8] is a route explanation, not a threat, insult or harassment; the complaint alleges overcharging only, no dangerous driving or injury. No SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 trigger → safety_concern = none.

Route deviation (RD-1 / RD-2). This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the meter follows distance, and the app quote of 10.6 km is not a fixed fare. The single off-route segment 09:13–09:24 drove 6.58 km where the optimal route covers 1.57 km, +5.01 km [F3], with +5.4 km / +50% overall [F1] and +10.3 min [F2].

Exemption check (RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5). There is no rider chat at all [F7] — no named stop (RD-3), no route consent before the detour (RD-5). The driver's post-trip statement that AYER Rajah Expressway was crawling [F8] is a claim, and it is also self-defeating on the facts: the traffic record shows the AYE congestion band 2 (10–19 km/h) only during 08:49–09:13 [F9], i.e. it ends exactly when the detour begins at 09:13, and did not cover the detour window. He does not name the road actually driven; the CE and Kent Ridge records [F10][F11] show no jamming in the detour window. No traffic incident is recorded near the optimal route [F12], so RD-4(a) is not satisfied, and a band-2 record on a different road/time cannot exempt under RD-4(b) (which in any case cannot exempt alone). Weather [F13] is a condition, not an RD-4 exemption, and it is likewise not tied to the detour window. The segment is therefore an unexempt detour (ground: consent_after_or_none), and RD-1 is breached.

Amount (RD-2). Rate = fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km = 22.50 ÷ 15.96 = $1.4098/km [F6]. The segment's extra_km is 5.01 (measured optimal-route coverage 1.57 km subtracted) [F3]. Refund = 5.01 × 1.4098 = $7.06 → $7.07. The GPS-level excess of 5.4 km / $7.53 [F1][F4] is not used in full, because RD-2 refunds only the sum of the unexempt segment extra_km; the remaining corridor/round-trip mileage is not refundable. Waiting time was $0.00 [F6], so no RD-3(c) waiting issue.

Flag (RD-6). RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; the driver's profiles show 3 disputes with 2 upheld but route: 0 [F15]. The RD-6 threshold is therefore not met, and profile facts cannot decide the case alone, so no flag_account. Driver's account-review point is noted for Ryde only as an observation, not a flag.

segment_findings.reason: No rider message exists before the segment [F7], so there is no RD-3 named stop and no RD-5 consent; the driver's post-trip statement about the AYE [F8] is a claim and is contradicted by the record, since the AYE band-2 congestion [F9] ends at 09:13 exactly when the detour starts and no incident is recorded on the optimal route [F12]. RD-4(a) is not met and the segment is an unexempt detour under RD-1/RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's after-the-fact statement of heavy rain/AYE congestion: consent and reasonable-cause excuses must be evidenced before/at the detour; the traffic record shows the AYE band-2 window 08:49–09:13 ends when the detour starts (09:13) and no incident is recorded near the optimal route [F9][F12], so the 'reasonable cause' claim for the detour window fails.

GPS-level +5.4 km / +50% excess is not the refund basis; RD-2 refunds only the unexempt segment's extra_km (5.01 km), not the whole GPS excess, since corridor/round-trip mileage within the 200 m corridor is not refundable.
Driver profile (2 upheld disputes, route: 0) does not satisfy RD-6's route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 and cannot independently establish the deviation or a flag.
